topic: AI basics: why AI can sound sure and still be wrong
post:
AI can sound 100% sure and still be wrong. 😬
There's a name for it, and 3 simple habits that help.

It's called a "hallucination":
when an AI gives an answer that sounds confident but isn't true.

Why it happens, in plain English:
AI writes by predicting what words should come next. Most of the time that's right. Sometimes it fills a gap with something that only sounds right.

Anthropic's own guide for Claude suggests a few habits that make this much less likely:

1️⃣ Give it permission to say "I don't know"
2️⃣ Ask it to quote the exact source text first
3️⃣ Tell it to use only the documents you gave it

Try adding this to your next prompt:
"Only use the attached document. Quote the exact lines you rely on. If the answer isn't in there, say 'I don't know.'"

Why it matters:
These habits reduce mistakes, but don't remove them. For anything important (numbers, names, dates, policies), you still check.
